summary: Configured node1 as an L2 switch with a VLAN-aware Linux bridge (br0): eth1 (link to node2) is an untagged access port in VLAN 100, eth2 (link to node3) is an untagged access port in VLAN 200. Each VLAN got its own SVI (br0.100 = 192.168.50.1/24, br0.200 = 192.168.51.1/24) so node1 keeps a working link to each host inside its own VLAN, while per-interface IPv4 forwarding is disabled on both SVIs so the two hosts cannot reach each other even via an explicit route. Config was persisted via a systemd oneshot unit (vlan-segmentation.service) that recreates br0/VLAN membership/SVIs/forwarding sysctls at boot. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (node1 first, then node2, then node3) using native reboot, boot_id changes were captured proving each restart actually occurred, and full VLAN segmentation + per-host connectivity + cross-VLAN isolation were reverified after each restart.
actions_performed: Mapped topology: node1 eth1<->node2 eth1, node1 eth2<->node3 eth1 (confirmed via temporary IP/ping test)
Assigned static IPs on node2 eth1 (192.168.50.2/24) and node3 eth1 (192.168.51.2/24) via nmcli (persisted ifcfg files, autoconnect=yes)
Attempted SONiC 'config vlan' CLI; failed because eth1/eth2 are not registered front-panel ports in configdb
Created VLAN-aware Linux bridge br0 on node1, attached eth1 and eth2, set eth1 PVID/untagged VLAN 100 and eth2 PVID/untagged VLAN 200, removed default VLAN 1 membership
Created SVI sub-interfaces br0.100 (192.168.50.1/24) and br0.200 (192.168.51.1/24) as node1's per-VLAN presence
Disabled net.ipv4.conf.br0.100.forwarding and net.ipv4.conf.br0.200.forwarding to prevent inter-VLAN routing between the two segments
Verified node1 reaches node2 and node3, and that node2 cannot reach node3's segment even with an explicit static route
Wrote /usr/local/bin/vlan-segmentation.sh and systemd unit vlan-segmentation.service (enabled, multi-user.target) on node1 to persist the VLAN config across reboot
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via 'reboot', polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, verified VLAN config/service auto-recreated and both segment links worked
Restarted node2 via 'sudo reboot', confirmed boot_id changed, verified eth1 link and ping to node1 recovered
Restarted node3 via 'sudo reboot', confirmed boot_id changed, verified eth1 link and ping to node1 recovered
Re-verified cross-VLAN isolation (node2 cannot reach node3 segment) after all restarts completed

evidence.summary: node1 pings 192.168.50.2 (node2, VLAN100 SVI) and 192.168.51.2 (node3, VLAN200 SVI) successfully, including post-restart

evidence.requirement: The two hosts (node2, node3) stay separated from one another
evidence.summary: node2 given explicit route to node3's subnet via node1; ping still 100% loss both before and after all node restarts, proving per-VLAN forwarding is disabled and segments are isolated
